feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles, with clear domain focus and solid evidence of progression and scope. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by adding more outcomes and trimming overlap.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility signals: long tenure at NACo, internal progression, recognizable tools, and meaningful scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Broad, relevant scope: combines strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI/search work in a way that feels current and differentiated.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add clearer results: several bullets describe responsibilities well but would be stronger with measurable outcomes (engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Tighten style consistency: use parallel bullet phrasing throughout, and standardize punctuation around lists. Minor style issues include “social, and multimedia” (remove comma), “Ranked among the top public universities…” (unnecessary filler), and mixed emphasis between strategic leadership and hands-on execution.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and recent roles.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and make the value proposition more direct: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years building platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel, punchier structure: “Specializes in enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled user experiences.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker from recent experience for impact, e.g., “10,000+ page websites” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Use consistent phrasing: “AI-enabled user experiences” is strong; keep “multimedia operations” over “production” if you want a more leadership-oriented tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems…” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Public-sector communications” is already implied by multiple NACo roles; avoid repeating it elsewhere in the header/subtitle.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized differentiators and used tighter, less generic phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad labels with more distinctive, outcome-oriented terms: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI search and structured content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Video, livestream and studio operations
- Use parallel phrasing throughout; avoid mixing “systems,” “operations,” and “experiences” inconsistently.
- Consider shortening “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI search and structured content discovery” for clarity and specificity.
- If targeting digital leadership roles, prioritize the most senior/recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI, then multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid mirroring exact wording.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets and may be redundant unless it’s a target-role keyword.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the language and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from work experience.
- Make each item more specific with scope, audience, or result: e.g., “for a national membership organization,” “Drupal 10 campaign microsite,” “conference installation tied to web content.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure: start each bullet with a strong verb and keep lists consistent (e.g., “Designed… Built… Developed… Produced…”).
- Revise for concision: “10×20-foot” should be “10 x 20-foot,” and “bill-level AI chat” may read more clearly as “bill-specific AI chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series overlap with the current freelance and NACo role bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may be the best differentiator if kept because it adds a unique experiential/digital integration example.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by emphasizing outcomes, level of ownership, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel coordination and publishing efficiency.
- Add measurable signals where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search/discovery improvements, reduced publishing time, or engagement gains.
- Use stronger ownership verbs: “Led,” “Designed,” “Built,” “Implemented,” “Established,” rather than “Support” or “Advise.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet brief unless you remove the footer project.
- Drupal microsites/storytelling/toolkits also overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite”; avoid repeating the same detail twice.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized outcomes and if channel oversight bullets were consolidated to avoid repeating themes covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with a tighter impact summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and operational improvements for a high-volume public-sector communications program.”
- Tighten the website bullet to foreground transformation and scale: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email open/click growth, follower growth, engagement rates, production volume, or cost/time saved if available.
- Combine analytics/governance into one operational-improvement bullet if space is tight: “Built analytics and governance systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, publishing standards, and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this one focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets; emphasize first-time in-house capability and organizational impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later NACo director role and the earlier digital media role. Make it more role-specific by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the broader strategic ownership in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, strengthening editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” are repeated across multiple NACo roles; keep this version operational, not strategic.
- Avoid repeating website/email/social oversight language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the summary and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent leadership scope.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with tighter, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better match the header language.
- “Editorial systems and governance” is solid, but “content operations” may feel more current and action-oriented.
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to scale, e.g., “enterprise web and content governance” or “high-volume stakeholder communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item repeats several phrases already in the header and Core Competencies, especially “digital strategy,” “multi-channel communication,” and “advocacy communication.”
- Avoid adding analytics or platform terms here; those are already covered well in other Topline Skills sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. It should emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint, WordPress & Power Pages • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first, since they align most clearly with the 2022–present experience.
- Tighten wording: change “AI-enabled search experiences” to “AI-enabled search” or “AI search implementation” for brevity.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “Enterprise Drupal platforms” or “Large-scale CMS migration support” to connect skills to demonstrated outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; avoid repeating the exact same platform list in both places.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack that aligns with the most recent leadership role, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize how you used analytics to drive decisions, not just the platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capabilities + business use: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, and digital performance optimization”
- Group tools more cleanly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboards and decision-support reporting”
- Consider a tighter version: “Analytics strategy & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Executive dashboards • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- The NACo Director role already names these tools; this skills item should summarize capability, not restate the same list too heavily.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list rather than a senior-level capability statement. It should better reflect recent leadership impact from NACo and avoid repeating “Multimedia & live event production” already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tasks/tools to outcomes-oriented capabilities: “Broadcast video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “PTZ camera systems,” “Virtual event production.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast video production & editing • Livestream, hybrid & virtual event delivery • PTZ camera systems • Studio buildout & operations”
- If space allows, elevate leadership scope with wording like “in-house studio operations” or “broadcast-quality production” to align with your 2022–2024 role.
- Keep only the most marketable terms; “video production and editing” + “livestreaming” can be condensed for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; vary the phrasing or remove one.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are closely related; combine to reduce repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize platform administration/modernization rather than repeat keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web CMS Administration: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light context instead of just tools: Enterprise CMS administration • platform migrations • modular content publishing
- Put Drupal first and keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was minor or older.
- Match phrasing to impact elsewhere: use “CMS administration” or “platform modernization” to align with recent Drupal-led work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [2]; consider removing GitHub Pages here or replacing this item with a narrower label like “CMS Platforms.”
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid adding another generic descriptor without differentiation.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tools by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools that support recent experience; consider adding scope if accurate, e.g., “tag management” instead of just “Google Tag Manager”
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Tag management (Google Tag Manager) • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD and deployment workflows (GitHub Actions)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- If Topline Skills stays detailed, this item should be shorter or more tool-specific to avoid repetition

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped, purpose-led categories: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue tracking: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add a short qualifier tied to recent work: “Used to build editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and communications workflow systems.”
- Put the most differentiating tools first; Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier matter more than Slack/Teams.
- Consider shortening the title to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and stronger alignment with your recent systems/governance work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating identical phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are lower-value if space is tight; collaboration tools can be trimmed first.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should better signal level of use and align with the strong email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Newsletter publishing • Audience segmentation
- If accurate, add a proficiency cue such as: “Enterprise and association email platforms” or “Platform administration and campaign deployment”
- Keep it platform-focused; let the work experience carry the scale and outcomes

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “analytics,” “workflow,” or broad digital strategy language here; those are already covered in Core Competencies and recent roles
- Don’t repeat audience size or newsletter scale in this skills item since that impact is already stronger in Work Experience

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo/consulting bullets. Use it to sharpen technical specificity rather than repeat broad capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with more technical/functional wording: “GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing”
- Cut “Dashboarding”; it’s implied by Looker Studio/Power BI and already echoed in “analytics and reporting infrastructure.”
- If accurate, add one higher-value specialty instead of a generic term: “KPI design,” “conversion tracking,” “event taxonomy,” or “reporting automation.”
- Keep the list concise and ordered by strategic value/recent use: GA4/BigQuery/reporting stack first, then Clarity/SEO/testing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating generic descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building, platform refresh support, and early multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support day-to-day operations across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact digital content” with concrete outputs: mention livestream production, weekly video updates, website refresh support, and workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or size/timeline of the website refresh.
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” rather than “guidance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early producing the series if true.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo entries unless you can specify what was improved.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support plus the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to foreground the standout outcome: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams, translating project work into digital and multimedia content.”
- Tighten the second sentence to one concrete achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production coordination and episode delivery.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a more concise final version: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo program and policy priorities; translated findings into digital and multimedia content. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize multimedia leadership here if video/studio growth is already established in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already established in recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize tools/software rather than broad capabilities.

Suggested edit
- Split software from production capabilities; keep this line tool-focused and concise.
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing • Livestream production support”
- If accurate, add level or context for the most relevant tools: “Adobe Premiere Pro (video editing)” or “Audition (audio cleanup/editing).”
- If you can show impact elsewhere, keep this item lean and let work experience carry outcomes.
